Perenco SA Insolvency Sends Shockwaves Through Panama’s Oil and Gas Sector

Panama City – Perenco SA, a major player in Panama’s Oil & Gas Producers sector, has entered insolvency proceedings, sending ripples through the country’s energy industry and raising concerns about the stability of key supply chains. The company, which operates extensive upstream facilities across the region, filed for bankruptcy protection earlier this week, citing a combination of depressed global oil prices and mounting operational costs.

The insolvency process is still ongoing, but immediate effects have already been felt across Perenco SA’s operations. Production at the company’s flagship Cerro Verde field has been scaled back by nearly 60%, with several drilling rigs standing idle. Company officials confirmed that a “substantial portion” of the workforce had been placed on unpaid leave pending further developments.

“We are facing unprecedented challenges and are working closely with administrators to safeguard as many jobs and assets as possible,” said Miguel Torres, Perenco SA’s Chief Operating Officer, at a press briefing Thursday. “Our priority is to maintain operational integrity where feasible while complying with the legal requirements of the insolvency process.”

The National Oil Producers Association of Panama expressed concern over the knock-on effects on local suppliers and service companies. “Perenco SA’s financial distress threatens not only direct jobs but also the hundreds of smaller contractors who depend on their business,” said association spokesperson Isabel Arias.

Local analysts estimate that Perenco SA accounted for roughly 22% of Panama’s oil output last year. The company’s difficulties have already led to a tightening of crude supplies in the domestic market, prompting some refineries to announce reduced throughput for the coming month.

Trade unions representing oil workers have called for government intervention to support affected employees. “We urge the authorities to ensure that workers’ rights are protected during this uncertain period,” said Julio Melendez, leader of the Panamanian Energy Workers’ Federation.

Despite the ongoing turmoil, administrators have reassured stakeholders that essential safety and environmental monitoring activities are continuing at all Perenco SA sites. A full assessment of the company’s financial position is expected to be completed within weeks, providing greater clarity on the future of its operations and workforce.
